analysis: Examined: ModelLoadAdmission.swift (head; only doc comment changed at 45-50, no logic change). SystemMemory.swift: the default `reclaimable` policy now reports max(free+inactive, free-speculative+external+purgeable) (head 60-87). This can only raise reported availability versus base (base 55-61), loosening load/KV admission on the provider's own machine. This is local availability/accounting, not a trust-boundary regression. free-only semantics are unchanged, including invalid env→freeOnly and failure→0 (head 13-16, 57-58). The 32-bit counter sums cannot overflow UInt64, and the subtraction is guarded by min. Integration could confirm that external_page_count and purgeable_count do not overlap on macOS, which would only affect over-admission. GLM5NextManagedLoad.swift adds phase timing, logging of model ID, file count and durations (no prompt data, head 181-182), and post-load PageCache.drop of .safetensors (head 175-177). It also adds verifiedArtifactSHA256 = catalog manifest aggregate, set only on the success path after aux verify (134), native core verify (286-291) and plan.weights.recheck (162, 318). Callers in other batches may publish this instead of rehashing (T-012/T-027/SEC-007 weight-hash). Integration must verify that callers read it only from a successful load and do not substitute it when unset. They must also confirm GLM5NextArtifactLoader really hashes every core file. That loader is not supplied. Weight hashes remain provider self-reported, so this is not a new trust grant. DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment.swift adds DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE to operationalKeys (head 16), so qualification is no longer refused when it is set. Its consumer is not supplied. If this file caches verification results that let a load skip hashing, an operator-writable path could spoof verification state (T-012/T-013). It could also alter qualification timing. Integration should check the file's location, ownership checks and whether it bypasses hashing. FlintResponseFormat.swift: only metadata was supplied. The file_changes range map shows requireExplicitTypes removed (base 36, 46-64), so untyped response_format leaves may compile as `string`. This is a correctness/contract concern, not a security control, but its source was not reviewed and no line is citable. No concrete regression is identified from the visible evidence.
